L5: # Gold Nanoparticles - Active Enrollment
L6: 
L7: We are conducting a trial for utilizing gold nanoparticles paired with infrared laser heat. Eligible patients have to have superficial tumors. We are treating the following types:
L8: 
L9: 【4†Image†images.squarespace-cdn.com】
L10: 
L11:   * Dogs with large mast cell tumors (>2 cm)
L12: 
L13:   * Dogs with soft tissue sarcomas (<2cm in diameter)
L14: 
L15:   * Dogs with oral melanoma (2-3cm diameter)
L16: 
L17:   * Dogs with cutaneous or footpad melanoma (<2cm)
L18:   * Cats with oral squamous cell carcinoma not involving the bone
L19: 
L20:   * Cats with other cutaneous tumors like Mast cell tumors, Sarcomas or Carcinomas
L21: 
L22: This clinical trial utilizes gold nanoparticles in a gross disease setting.
L23: Gold Nanoparticles are inert and are given IV to the patient and after a period of time the patient comes back to have the tumor heated with a laser. As the tumor vasculature is heated through the external near infrared spectrum of light, the gold nanoparticles are excited, the laser energy is converted to heat and the tumor vasculature is disrupted killing the tumor from the inside out.
L24: Smaller tumors typically need only the 1 session of heat but larger tumors may need more than 1 session of heat (average 2-3 for sarcomas).
L25: 
L26: THE TRIAL IS NOW ENROLLING PATIENTS!
L27: 
L28: If you have a potential case to discuss, have a patient with a tumor in a bad location for surgery or if you would like to learn more, please contact us at 425-697-2272 for more information.
L29: # Gilvetmab paired with EGFR for Histo diagnosed Hemangiosarcoma - CLOSED
L30: 
L31: 
L32: 
L33: The current clinical trial for EGFR vaccination with Yale has been granted the rights to add Gilvetmab for these patients through a MERCK Product Grant Support. These patients received Gilvetmab paired with Carboplatin and EGFR. We will now be looking at dogs with Carboplatin and EGFR as the comparison arm.
L34: #  Paclitaxel for K9 Hemangiosarcoma - CLOSED
L35: 
L36: BARC was enrolling patients in a clinical trial for a unique chemotherapy agent for splenic hemangiosarcoma patients but we have reached the enrollment goal and the trial is now closed. The company that produces Paclitaxel will be evaluating the results in hopes to bring the drug to market.
L37: 
L38: Trial Status: CLOSED FOR DATA REVIEW
L39: # Paclitaxel for Feline Tumors - CLOSED
L40: 
L41: BARC was enrolling Feline patients in a clinical trial for Paclitaxel in a variety of tumor types. The company that produces Paclitaxel will be evaluating the results in hopes to bring the drug to market.
L42: 
L43: Trial Status: CLOSED FOR DATA REVIEW
L44: # Study for Canine Lymphoma - CLOSED
L45: 
L46: We just completed the enrollment for this novel immunotherapy in dogs with Naive B cell lymphoma or Refractory B cell lymphoma. Once the dose finding data has been evaluated we are hopeful a second arm of the trial may be available for patients with B cell lymphoma to look at efficacy.
L47: 
L48: Financial Support: Fully funded. All treatments and procedures associated with the clinical trial will occur with no cost to the owner.
L49: 
L50: Trial Status: CLOSED FOR DATA REVIEW
L51: # TLR 7,8,9 Immunotherapy - Coming soon
L52: 
L53: BARC is going to be enrolling patients in a clinical trial for a unique immunotherapy for gross disease sarcomas and carcinomas. We anticipate this trial being open in September 2026.
L54: 
L55: Trial Status: COMING SOON
L56: #  Randomized trial of Fecal Transplant with Palladia for multiple tumor types - COMING SOON
L57: We will be looking at whether receiving fecal transplant capsules at the same time as Palladia can improve the microbiome in dogs and potentially reduce the side effect profile of Palladia. Dogs receiving Palladia naively will enroll to receive fecal transplant capsules or placebo but active Palladia. The first 3 months of the Palladia administration, additional samples will be collected from the patient to determine how the microbiome adjusts during this timeframe.
L58: 
L59: Trial Status: COMING SOON
L60: # Study for Canine Superficial Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) - Active Enrollment
L61: 
L62: * * *
L63: We are enrolling pet companion dogs that have been diagnosed with non-metastatic squamous cell carcinoma (SCC, a type of cancer) in a clinical trial for a newly formulated chemotherapy treatment delivered via an intratumor injection. An intratumor injection requires a much lower dose of carboplatin than required by administration systemically. Additionally, this new formulation hopes to provide long-acting local activity.
L64: 
L65: Eligibility for Dogs to Participate in the Study include but are not limited to:
L66: · The dog is diagnosed cytologically or histologically with Squamous cell carcinoma.
L67: 
L68: · The dog has at least one lesion with a longest diameter (LD) of ≥1.0 cm that can be measured to assess response to treatment.
L69: 
L70: · The dog has no evidence of metastasis based on thoracic radiographs and cytological evaluation of local lymph nodes, and any palpably enlarged lymph nodes.
L71: 
L72: · The dog has not received prior treatment with radiation, immunotherapy, or chemotherapy for cancer.
L73: · The dog has no renal, cardiovascular, hepatic, and/or gastrointestinal dysfunction, neutropenia, or thrombocytopenia.
L74: 
L75: · The dog has no uncontrolled systemic disorders (such as diabetes mellitus) other than SCC.
L76: 
L77: · The dog has no significant co-morbid illness, which includes but is not limited to a history of congestive heart failure or clinical coagulopathy.
L78: 
L79: Financial Support: Fully funded. All treatments and procedures associated with the clinical trial will occur with no cost to the owner.
L80: Trial Status: Currently Ongoing
L81: 
L82: 【5†Image†images.squarespace-cdn.com】
L83: # EGFR Immunotherapy - Active Enrollment
L84: 
L85: BARC continues to offer a unique immunotherapy that targets the EGFR/HER2 pathway. Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) is overexpressed on a number of human cancers, and often is indicative of a poor outcome.
L86: 
L87: We are hoping to induce a polyclonal anti-EGFR/HER2 tumor antigen response by vaccine therapy.
L88: We are enrolling companion dogs with spontaneous EGFR expressing tumors to receive a series of 2 vaccines 3 weeks apart. There is another visit after vaccination to draw a blood sample for antigen response analysis. Dogs with EGFR expressing tumors will be immunized with a short peptide of the EGFR extracellular domain with sequence homology to HER2.
L89: 
L90: To receive the immunotherapy without required Oncologist consultation:
L91: 1. Referral direct from another Veterinary Specialist (Oncologist, Internist, Surgeon, etc)
L92: 
L93: 2. Viable tumor types include:
L94: 
L95:   * Osteosarcoma patients
L96: 
L97:   * Hemangiosarcoma patients
L98: 
L99:   * Transitional Cell Carcinoma
L100: 
L101:   * Pulmonary Carcinoma (with records review)
L102: 
L103:   * High grade Mast cell tumors (with records review)
L104: 
L105: Naive patients can also schedule to have an Oncology consult and this therapy will be discussed if applicable to your dogs disease profile.
L106: 
L107: Please contact us today for more information!

L207: Vivesto is a Swedish drug development company that aims to offer new treatment options for hard-to-treat cancers where there are major medical needs and significant market potential. The project portfolio consists of Cantrixil, which is being developed for blood cancer, and the veterinary oncology program Paccal Vet (paclitaxel micellar), which is being evaluated in a pilot clinical trial in dogs with splenic hemangiosarcoma following splenectomy and in a dose-finding study in cats with solid tumors.
L208: Vivesto’s shares are traded on Nasdaq Stockholm (ticker: VIVE).

L181: # Atherton Laboratory
L182: 
L183: ## Our Research
L184: 
L185: We are interested in defining the prognostic and therapeutic role of T cells in hematologic malignancies utilizing a multispecies comparative approach. Our research involves identification and appraisal of novel strategies for T cell-based immunotherapy in clinical trials of canine cancer patients with tumors bearing translational importance for human medicine.
L186: 
L187: 【63†Learn more about our research】
L188: 
L189: * * *
L190: 
L191: ## Clinical Trials
L192: #### Evaluation of Novel CAR T Therapy for Canine Histiocytic Sarcoma
L193: In this study we will investigate the safety and therapeutic activity of a type of engineered white blood cell known as a CAR T cell.  CAR T cells are made from T cells collected from your dog. In this study, we will engineer T cells to express a cancer targeting receptor known as a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR). The CAR directs the modified T cells to the cancer cells which are then killed.
L194: The purpose of this study is to determine the safety of CAR T cells, their maximum tolerated dose, how long they will remain in the patient and their effectiveness against histiocytic sarcoma.
L195: For more information, please email mattath@upenn.edu.
L196: ## News and Publications
L197: #### Atherton Lab News
L198: 
L199: May 2026 | Luiza Cesar Conti received the Wim Misdorp Research Award at the European Society of Veterinary Oncology Annual  Congress for presentation of “Bivalent loop CAR T cells exert specific effector function against canine B cells” in Dublin. Congratulations, Luiza!
L200: June 7, 2024 | Katie Bardales received ACVIM Resident Research Award for presenting the lab’s studies of the transcriptional immune microenvironment in canine mast cell tumors in Minneapolis. Congratulations, Katie!
L201: 
L202: June 6, 2024 | Matt Atherton received a travel award for presenting the lab’s comparative studies of osteopontin in histiocytic sarcoma at the 6th International Conference on Cytokines in Cancer in Greece.
L203: 
L204: May 23, 2024 | The Atherton Lab welcomes new members Dr. Lang Jiang and Lizzy Fiepke!
L205: July 19, 2024 | Philadelphia Inquirer featured Penn Vet’s 【64†canine cancer research†www.inquirer.com】
L206:
